question: Michigan Democratic Senate Primary Winner
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Democratic Primary for United States Senator from Michigan.

If no 2026 Michigan Democratic Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the Michigan Democratic party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

"Other" means any option not listed here.
research:
I could only use sources dated on or before 2026-07-25. Some searches brought up later articles, and I left those out completely.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the Michigan Democratic Party's first announcement of results, or on an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting. No URL is given. The primary is on August 4, 2026, so as of 2026-07-25 there are no results to report. [Ballotpedia](https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate_election_in_Michigan,_2026_(August_4_Democratic_primary))

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. In practice it is a two-way race between Abdul El-Sayed and Haley Stevens.
- 2026-07-05: Mallory McMorrow suspended her campaign without endorsing anyone. Her name stays on the August 4 ballot because ballots had already been printed and mailed to absentee voters. [Michigan Advance](https://michiganadvance.com/2026/07/05/mcmorrow-withdraws-from-u-s-senate-race/), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/michigan-democrat-mallory-mcmorrow-drops-out-senate-race-weeks-before-primary)
- Dana Nessel, Rashida Tlaib, Sarah Anthony and Kristen McDonald Rivet are not running in this race. Nessel endorsed Stevens after McMorrow left, and Tlaib backs El-Sayed. [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/michigan-democrat-mallory-mcmorrow-drops-out-senate-race-weeks-before-primary), [TIME](https://time.com/article/2026/07/16/new-polling-after-mcmorrow-s-exit-shake-up-michigan-senate-race/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-07-16: TIME reports three polls taken after McMorrow's exit:
  - Detroit News/WDIV (Glengariff, July 8-11): Stevens 48%, El-Sayed 41%.
  - Tavern Research: Stevens ahead by 1 point.
  - Data for Progress: El-Sayed ahead by 13. This poll was paid for by a pro-El-Sayed super PAC.

  [TIME](https://time.com/article/2026/07/16/new-polling-after-mcmorrow-s-exit-shake-up-michigan-senate-race/)
- 2026-07-13: Retiring Sen. Gary Peters endorsed Stevens. El-Sayed is backed by the UAW, Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Tlaib and Andy Levin. [TIME](https://time.com/article/2026/07/16/new-polling-after-mcmorrow-s-exit-shake-up-michigan-senate-race/)
- 2026-07-08: Michigan Advance reports a Tavern Research poll (online, n=2,211, MOE ±2.5) showing the two statistically tied. Another summary of the same Tavern poll (July 6-7) gives El-Sayed 41%, Stevens 38%. El-Sayed has the better net favorability, 45% to 40%. [Michigan Advance](https://michiganadvance.com/2026/07/08/new-poll-shows-el-sayed-stevens-statistically-tied-in-michigans-democratic-u-s-senate-primary/)
- 2026-07-08: Newsweek cites two late-June polls:
  - Quantus Insights (June 29-30): El-Sayed 41%, Stevens 36%.
  - Tulchin Research (June 24-28): El-Sayed 46%, Stevens 27%.

  Pollster Bernie Porn thinks McMorrow's exit helps Stevens more. [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/abdul-el-sayed-chances-winning-michigan-primary-mcmorrow-ends-race-12160118)
- 2026-07-05: According to a person with direct knowledge, a recent wave of outside spending supporting Stevens was the main reason McMorrow left, as reported by ABC/AP. [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/US/wireStory/democrat-mallory-mcmorrow-suspends-michigan-senate-campaign-scrambles-134501094)
- Before the exit: an Emerson/WOOD-TV poll had El-Sayed and McMorrow tied at 24%, Stevens at 13%, and 36% undecided. [Emerson](https://emersoncollegepolling.com/michigan-2026-poll-abdul-el-sayed-mallory-mcmorrow-tied-for-lead-in-democratic-senate-primary/)

## 4. Base rates
- Open-seat Senate primaries where the establishment and progressive wings face off are often close, and this race's polls disagree a lot by sponsor. Since July 5, independent polls range from Stevens +7 to El-Sayed +3, and sponsored polls reach El-Sayed +13.
- I could not find a clean statistical base rate for how often the poll leader three weeks out goes on to win a Senate primary like this one.
- McMorrow will get some residual votes because her name is still on the ballot, but she has no real path to winning.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Earlier in the cycle, Polymarket had El-Sayed at about 52%, McMorrow at 30% and Stevens at 14%. [Action Network](https://www.actionnetwork.com/politics/michigan-democratic-senate-primary-winner-odds-predictions-polymarket)
- April 2026: a post on X put Kalshi at McMorrow 53%, El-Sayed 33%, Stevens 16%. [X/Ben Freeman](https://x.com/benwfreeman1/status/2044455485143740715)
- July 4-8, 2026:
  - Polymarket: El-Sayed fell from 87% to 78%, and Stevens rose from 13% to 20%.
  - Kalshi: El-Sayed went from 87.8% to about 83%, and Stevens from 11% to 19%.

  [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/abdul-el-sayed-chances-winning-michigan-primary-mcmorrow-ends-race-12160118)
- I could not find a verified market price dated July 20-25. The most recent pre-cutoff figures have El-Sayed at roughly 78-83%.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late July: more public polls are expected, and a candidate debate may happen before the primary.
- Ongoing: outside spending (pro-Israel groups and super PACs backing Stevens, a pro-El-Sayed PAC) and the attack ads that come with it.
- Ongoing: absentee and early voting, including ballots already cast for McMorrow. Voters can spoil a ballot only in limited cases. [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/michigan-democrat-mallory-mcmorrow-drops-out-senate-race-weeks-before-primary)
- 2026-08-04: primary day. Results usually come in that night or the next morning. Media calls (AP) will probably come before any announcement from the state party.
